explanation: Sort the characters of both strings and compare the resulting sequences. Equal sorted sequences have exactly the same character multiplicities.
timeComplexity: O(a log a + b log b) time for string lengths a and b. Sorting both character sequences dominates their final equality comparison.
spaceComplexity: O(a + b) auxiliary space. Character buffers or sorted copies hold both strings.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Sorting places equal characters together in a canonical order. Two strings produce the same sorted sequence exactly when every character has the same multiplicity, which is precisely the anagram condition.
walkthrough: Sort "cider" into "cdeir" and "cried" into "cdeir". The canonical sequences match, so return true.
edgeCases: Only lowercase English letters occur in this contract.
Different lengths cannot have equal multiplicities.
Repeated letters must have matching counts; two empty strings are anagrams.
